de_plosive.properties: Signal chain: Linkwitz-Riley 24 dB/oct crossover at Frequency (sums back flat) → detector on both channels: fast low- and high-band envelopes (1 ms / 30 ms) and a slow low-band average (200 ms); when the low band rises above both by more than the threshold it is cut by twice the excess, up to Max Reduction (1 ms attack, Release) → bands summed. slider_desc: Gain at 31 Hz (-18 to +18 dB): the sub and deep low end; drag the first point in the curve.
Gain at 63 Hz (-18 to +18 dB): kick and bass weight.
Gain at 125 Hz (-18 to +18 dB): bass body and warmth.
Gain at 250 Hz (-18 to +18 dB): low mids, where mud and boxiness build up.
Gain at 500 Hz (-18 to +18 dB): body of voices, guitars and snares.
Gain at 1 kHz (-18 to +18 dB): the centre of the midrange, nasal or honky when boosted.
Gain at 2 kHz (-18 to +18 dB): presence and attack.
Gain at 4 kHz (-18 to +18 dB): clarity and edge, harsh if pushed.
Gain at 8 kHz (-18 to +18 dB): brilliance and sibilance.
Gain at 16 kHz (-18 to +18 dB): air and sparkle (left out at sample rates below 36 kHz).

draw_eq.properties: Ten points at fixed octave-spaced frequencies (31.25 Hz to 16 kHz) set the gain the curve passes through. Each point drives an RBJ peaking filter; the ten gains are solved (Gaussian elimination on the filters' interaction, then two corrections with the true response) so the cascade passes through every point to within a fraction of a dB, and Smoothness sets the filters' Q from 1.5 to 0.6. sampler.properties: An instrument: MIDI in, stereo out, 16 voices (a 17th note takes the oldest released voice, else the oldest, with a 2 ms fade). Reads WAV and FLAC (mono, stereo; more channels play the first two) up to 4,194,304 sample values, at the file's own rate with 4-point Hermite interpolation. Linear attack and exponential decay/release, a TPT state-variable low-pass per voice with its own decaying envelope, loop with a declick of the jump, 3 ms fade at the sample's end, sustain pedal (CC 64), all notes off (CC 123), all sound off (CC 120), pitch bend. Without a file a deterministic built-in sound is generated, so it always makes sound.
